2 صمّتهُ , (M, A, K,) inf. n. تَصْمِيتٌ; (S;) and ↓ اصمتهُ ; (M, A, Msb, K;) He made him, or rendered him, silent, mute, or speechless: (S, A, Msb, K:) or he made him, or rendered him, long silent or mute or speechless. (M.) ―
-b2- [Hence,] صَمِّتِى صَبِيَّكِ Feed thy child with that which will silence it [or quiet it]. (A, TA.) ―
-b3- And صمّت الرَّجُلَ He inclined to the man who complained to him by reason of his complaint [and so quieted him; or he cared for the complaint of the man and so quieted him; see مُصَمِّتٌ]. (M, TA.) ＝
-A2- See also 1, first sentence.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
